comment_text.ja2:1.2: Resolve udaṅgaṇa as uda (“water”) and aṅgaṇa, from a root sense of “going”, from where we find the Sanskrit sense of “passage” (against the commentary, which says uda is a mere particle). In the prose story, the Bodhisatta, lost with his caravan in the desert, hears water rushing underground and urges a young man to dig.

translation_text.ja2:0.4: Sandy Waste: a past life story
translation_text.ja2:1.1: Digging untiringly in a sandy waste,
translation_text.ja2:1.2: there at the underground stream he found water.
translation_text.ja2:1.3: In the same way, a sage with strength aroused
translation_text.ja2:1.4: untiringly finds the peace of the heart.

variant_text.ja2:1.3: Evaṁ munī viriyabalūpapanno → muni vīriya … (sya1ed, sya2ed, mr); muni viriya … (pts-vp-pli1)
